title: Supply Chain Finance for Ethiopian Exports and Imports
subtitle: Finance whole value chains from farm gate to foreign buyer on receivables, goods and anchor strength, not only buildings
summary: Design, price and control anchor-led supply chain finance, inventory and warehouse receipt finance, and export and import programmes, using one Ethiopian brewery and its 300 suppliers as the running case.
audience: Trade and transaction banking product managers, corporate relationship managers and experienced trade, SME and agricultural finance officers in Ethiopian banks who have completed the Level 1 course or have equivalent experience.
objectives: Design a supply chain finance programme anchored on a large buyer or exporter
Assess risks and structure limits, pricing and controls for programme finance
Finance commodities and inventory against registered security, collateral management and ECX warehouse receipts
Structure export and import SCF within Ethiopia's foreign exchange rules
Build partnerships with anchors, collateral managers, insurers and guarantee providers

runningCase.name: Meskerem Malt and Beverage S.C.
runningCase.text: Meskerem Malt and Beverage S.C. runs a brewery and malt plant near Asella with annual revenue of about ETB 9.2 billion. It buys about ETB 2.4 billion a year of malting barley, packaging, transport and maintenance services from 300 suppliers: 220 smallholder barley growers organised through four primary cooperatives, and 80 SMEs. It pays on 60-day terms and wants 90 days, but its suppliers already wait for cash, and some farmers sell barley to traders at a discount for quick payment. Bank A, Meskerem's main bank, is designing a payables finance programme for the 300 suppliers, an inventory facility for the barley union that aggregates their harvest, and distributor finance on the sales side. Each module takes the design one step further, to a credit committee presentation in Module 5.

modules.title: Designing an anchor-led programme
modules.summary: Map where cash gets stuck in a value chain, choose the right anchor and design how suppliers join, qualify and get paid.
objectives: Map an Ethiopian value chain and locate the finance gaps and risks at each stage
Distinguish the main supply chain finance products from a plain working capital loan
Select an anchor and size a programme from its spend, terms and supplier base
Set supplier onboarding and eligibility rules and choose a delivery platform

lessons.title: Where the cash gets stuck in a value chain
body: Supply chain finance starts with a map, not a product. Follow the goods and the money from the first producer to the final buyer, and mark every point where someone has delivered but not yet been paid, or has to pay before they can sell. Those points are the finance gaps.

In Ethiopia the classic chains are export chains (coffee, sesame, flowers, livestock, textiles) and import chains (fuel, fertiliser, medicines). In each, the strongest party, often a large exporter, processor, importer or brewery, sits near the end of the chain and has the best access to bank credit. The weakest, smallholders and small suppliers, carry the longest wait for cash.

A programme anchored on the strong party lets the bank lend to the weak parties on the strength of the anchor's payment promise or of the goods themselves, instead of demanding a building from each farmer or SME.

items.label: Farmer
items.text: Harvests red cherry; needs inputs and cash at harvest

items.label: Cooperative or washing station
items.text: Buys cherry for cash, processes, waits weeks to sell

items.label: Exporter
items.text: Buys at ECX or direct, cleans and bags, waits for shipment

items.label: Djibouti and shipping
items.text: Goods in transit for weeks; documents move to the buyer's bank

items.label: Foreign roaster
items.text: Pays on documents or on credit terms; proceeds return within the FX window

example.title: Mapping a Sidama coffee chain
example.text: In the Level 1 exercise, learners followed coffee from Wenago Ridge Farmers' Cooperative to a roaster in Hamburg through Sidra Highland Coffee Export PLC. They found three gaps: the cooperative pays farmers in cash at harvest but sells weeks later, the exporter buys and cleans before it ships, and the roaster pays 30 days after documents. Bank A could offer inventory finance to the cooperative against stored parchment, pre-shipment finance to the exporter against an authenticated sales contract, and an advance against export bills once the goods are on their way.

lessons.tip: Draw the money line under the goods line. The finance gaps are where the two lines are furthest apart.

lessons.title: The SCF product family and how it differs from a loan
body: A plain loan is underwritten on the borrower's balance sheet and secured, in Ethiopian practice, mostly by buildings. Supply chain finance is underwritten on a specific trade flow: an approved invoice, a sales contract, a letter of credit or goods held under control. Repayment comes from the flow itself, when the buyer pays or the goods are sold.

That changes three things. The tenor follows the trade cycle, often 30 to 180 days. The limit follows the volume of eligible trade, not the value of a title deed. And the bank's key risks become the buyer's payment, the genuineness of the trade and control of the goods.

items.label: Pre-shipment finance
items.text: Cash to buy and prepare exports against a contract or L/C

items.label: Receivables discounting and factoring
items.text: Supplier sells or pledges invoices before the buyer pays

items.label: Payables finance
items.text: Buyer-led: approved invoices paid early on the buyer's risk

items.label: Inventory and warehouse finance
items.text: Advance against goods under control or warehouse receipts

items.label: Distributor finance
items.text: Anchor-linked credit for distributors to buy stock

items.label: Documentary trade
items.text: L/Cs, collections and advances on import or export bills

points: Supplier-led products (discounting, factoring) rest on the supplier's credit plus the buyer's.
Buyer-led products (payables finance) rest mainly on the anchor's credit.
Asset-led products (inventory, warehouse receipts) rest on control of the goods.

lessons.title: Choosing the anchor
body: The anchor is the company whose strength carries the programme. It must be creditworthy enough that the bank is comfortable holding a large, short-term exposure on it, and it must buy enough, from enough suppliers, on predictable terms, to justify the set-up cost.

Good anchors in Ethiopia include breweries, malt and flour processors, edible oil refiners, large exporters, pharmaceutical and fuel importers and state enterprises with reliable payment records. A weak anchor makes the programme a concentrated loan to a weak name, whatever the number of suppliers.
points: Credit quality: audited statements, leverage, payment discipline with existing suppliers
Spend: annual purchases from the target suppliers and how stable they are
Supplier base: number, size, geography and how dependent they are on the anchor
Systems: can the anchor confirm invoices quickly and electronically
Motive: does the anchor want longer terms, supplier stability, or both

scenario.title: Three possible anchors
scenario.situation: Bank A's transaction banking team has budget for one new programme this year. Candidate 1 is a construction contractor with ETB 900 million of purchases, irregular project cash flow and two delayed supplier payments last year. Candidate 2 is Meskerem Malt and Beverage S.C., with ETB 2.4 billion of purchases from 300 suppliers and audited profits for six years. Candidate 3 is a garment exporter with ETB 300 million of purchases from 12 suppliers.
scenario.question: Which anchor best fits a payables finance programme?
options: The contractor, because its suppliers need cash the most
Meskerem, because of its credit strength, spend and broad supplier base
The garment exporter, because few suppliers are easier to manage
Any of them, as long as each supplier pledges a building
scenario.explain: Payables finance rests on the anchor's promise to pay. Meskerem combines a strong record with enough spend and suppliers to spread set-up costs. The contractor's irregular payments are exactly the risk the bank would be taking, and the exporter's spend is too small and concentrated.

example.title: Why an importer was turned down as anchor
example.text: Gonder Pharma Import PLC asked Bank A to finance its 40 pharmacy distributors on its name. Its audited accounts showed short-term debt of three times equity and a supplier dispute in court. The team declined the anchor role and instead offered the strongest distributors individual facilities with their own security.

lessons.title: Sizing the Meskerem programme
body: A programme limit is set from the expected financed volume and how long each invoice stays financed, plus headroom for seasonal peaks. Meskerem buys about ETB 2.4 billion a year from its 300 suppliers and wants to move from 60-day to 90-day terms. Bank A expects 60% of approved invoices to be discounted early, about 80 days before the due date on average.
The limit is an exposure on Meskerem, so it must sit inside the bank's single-counterparty limits together with Meskerem's existing overdraft and term loan.

worked.title: Meskerem payables finance: programme limit (ETB million)

rows.label: Annual eligible spend with the 300 suppliers

worked.note: Bank A proposes an ETB 400 million programme limit on Meskerem and will test it against large exposure rules in Module 2.

regulation.text: A bank's exposure to one counterparty or group of connected counterparties may not exceed 25% of its total capital. An exposure of 10% or more of total capital is a large exposure and is reported monthly within 20 days. A programme limit on an anchor counts toward that anchor's group exposure.

visual.caption: Size from trade volume and tenor, then check it against the anchor's total exposure.

lessons.title: Supplier onboarding and eligibility
body: Onboarding 300 suppliers is the hardest operational task in the programme. The anchor helps by introducing suppliers, sharing their supply history and explaining the offer, but the bank still owns customer due diligence, account opening and the supplier agreement.

Segment the suppliers. Meskerem's 80 SMEs (packaging, transport, crown corks, labels, maintenance) can sign individually. Its 220 smallholder barley growers are better onboarded through their four primary cooperatives, with farmers identified individually, ideally with their national digital ID, and paid into their own accounts.

items.label: Anchor nominates
items.text: Supplier list with 12 months of supply and payment history

items.label: Bank screens
items.text: Identity, trade licence and TIN for SMEs; ID and cooperative membership for farmers

items.label: Supplier signs
items.text: Supplier agreement: assignment of approved invoices, discount, fees

items.label: Account set-up
items.text: Bank account or wallet for payment; no cash disbursement

items.label: First invoice
items.text: Approved invoice uploaded by the anchor; supplier chooses early payment

points: Eligibility: at least 12 months supplying the anchor, no open quality disputes, clean credit report
Exclude related parties of the anchor unless approved under related party rules
Set a per-supplier cap so no single supplier dominates the programme

example.title: Onboarding through a cooperative
example.text: At Lemu Barley Growers' Cooperative near Bekoji, Bank A's team and Meskerem's procurement officer, Hirut Alemu, held a field day. In two days they opened accounts for 64 farmers, recorded their IDs and plot sizes, and had the cooperative chair sign a delivery-confirmation procedure, so each farmer's barley would be weighed and graded in their own name.

lessons.title: Programme documents and platform choice
body: Three documents carry the programme. The master agreement with the anchor contains its irrevocable undertaking to pay the full face value of every approved invoice on the due date, with no set-off after approval. The supplier agreement assigns approved invoices to the bank in return for early payment at a discount. The operating procedure sets who uploads, approves and pays, and by when.

The platform can be a controlled spreadsheet process for a pilot, a module in the bank's core system, or a specialist SCF platform connected to the anchor's ERP. With 300 suppliers and weekly invoice files, manual handling quickly creates errors and duplicate financing risk.

left.title: Manual or spreadsheet pilot
items: High risk of keying errors and duplicates

right.title: Platform linked to the anchor's ERP
items: Duplicate checks and audit trail built in

scenario.title: A set-off clause
scenario.situation: Meskerem's legal team asks to add a clause letting it deduct quality claims from approved invoices at maturity, even after Bank A has paid the supplier early. Meskerem's procurement head, Dawit Bekele, says rejected barley is common in wet seasons.
scenario.question: How should Bank A respond?
options: Accept, since quality claims are a normal part of trade
Insist that quality claims are settled before approval, and that approval makes payment irrevocable
Accept, but double the discount rate
Drop the programme because barley quality varies
scenario.explain: The anchor's irrevocable, no set-off undertaking after approval is what lets the bank price on the anchor's risk. Quality checks belong before approval; disputes after that are settled between anchor and supplier, not against the bank's payment.

takeaways: Map goods and money together; finance gaps sit where suppliers wait longest for cash
SCF is underwritten on a trade flow and repaid from it, not on a building
The anchor's credit, spend and supplier base decide whether a programme is viable
Size the limit from spend, uptake, days financed and seasonal headroom, then check large exposure rules
An irrevocable, no set-off payment undertaking after approval is the core of payables finance

quiz.q: What most distinguishes supply chain finance from a plain working capital loan?
options: It always has a longer tenor
It is underwritten on a specific trade flow and repaid from it
quiz.explain: SCF ties the credit to an invoice, contract or goods, and repayment comes when that trade settles.

quiz.q: In payables finance, whose credit risk does the bank mainly take?
quiz.explain: The anchor's irrevocable promise to pay approved invoices is the main source of repayment.

quiz.q: Meskerem's expected financed volume is ETB 1,440 million a year, each invoice financed for 80 days. What is the average outstanding?
quiz.explain: 1,440 x 80 / 365 is about ETB 315.6 million.

quiz.q: Under SBB/87/2024, a large exposure is one that is
quiz.explain: Large exposure means 10% or more of total capital; the cap per group is 25%.

quiz.q: Why are Meskerem's smallholders onboarded through their cooperatives?
options: It is the practical channel to identify, register and confirm deliveries for many small farmers
The anchor refuses to deal with farmers
Cooperatives become the borrowers instead of farmers
quiz.explain: The cooperative organises delivery and grading, while each farmer is still identified and paid individually.

quiz.q: Which clause in the anchor agreement most protects the bank?
options: A right to reject invoices after early payment
A right to extend payment by 30 days
An irrevocable undertaking to pay approved invoices in full with no set-off
quiz.explain: No set-off after approval lets the bank rely on the anchor's credit alone.

modules.title: Credit, risk, limits and pricing for programme finance
modules.summary: Assess the anchor and its suppliers, measure dilution, choose between true sale and recourse, and set limits and prices that hold up at committee.
objectives: Analyse the anchor's credit and the effect of longer payment terms on its balance sheet
Assess supplier performance risk, dilution and fraud, and set controls for each
Explain the difference between true sale and recourse structures and the Ethiopian legal steps behind them
Build a risk-based price for programme finance and defend it against cheaper alternatives

lessons.title: Anchor credit: the obligor behind every invoice
body: Every approved invoice in a payables programme is, in substance, a short-term exposure on the anchor. The bank analyses the anchor as it would for an overdraft: profitability, leverage, liquidity, cash conversion and payment record. Then it asks a second question: what happens to the anchor when it stretches suppliers from 60 to 90 days?

Longer terms free cash for the anchor, but some analysts treat programme payables as disguised debt. If the anchor's own cash is weak, the programme only postpones the problem and concentrates it on the bank.

worked.title: Meskerem: anchor credit check (ETB million)

rows.label: Cash freed by moving 60 to 90 days: 2,400 x 30 / 365
Net debt / EBITDA if programme payables were counted as debt: (3,100 + 316) / 1,840

worked.note: Meskerem stays comfortably within a 2.5x leverage covenant even if the programme is treated as debt, so the anchor risk is acceptable.

example.title: An anchor that used suppliers as a bank
example.text: Ambo Edible Oil Factory PLC moved its suppliers from 30 to 120 days through a programme at another lender. Its reported debt looked low, but when crude oil prices rose it could not pay the approved invoices on time. The lender had to classify the exposure and the suppliers lost confidence in the programme. The lesson: test the anchor's cash without the stretch, not only its reported leverage.

lessons.title: Supplier performance risk and fraud
body: Before the anchor approves an invoice, the supplier must deliver goods of the right quantity and quality. That is performance risk. In pre-approval products, such as purchase-order finance or receivables discounting, the bank carries it; in payables finance the anchor's approval removes most of it.

Fraud risk sits in the documents: invoices for goods never delivered, the same invoice financed twice, or invoices inflated with a collusive buyer officer. Controls are mostly systems controls: unique invoice numbers, approval only by named anchor staff, and payments only to the supplier's own account.

items.label: Non-delivery
items.text: Goods short, late or rejected; covered by approval before funding

items.label: Duplicate invoices
items.text: Same invoice financed twice; unique number and hash checks

items.label: Collusion
items.text: Anchor staff approve fake invoices; dual approval and rotation

items.label: Diversion
items.text: Payment to third parties; pay only to the supplier's own account

scenario.title: The same invoice twice
scenario.situation: Bank A's platform flags that Abdi Transport Services PLC uploaded an invoice for ETB 2.3 million, already financed by Bank A last month under a different number. Abdi explains it was a re-issued invoice after a correction.
scenario.question: What should the programme officer do first?
options: Report Abdi to the police immediately
Ask Abdi to pledge a building
Pay, since the anchor approved the second invoice
Hold the payment, confirm with Meskerem which invoice is valid, and cancel one
scenario.explain: Duplicate checks exist to stop double financing. The officer confirms the valid document with the anchor first; escalation follows if the explanation does not hold.

lessons.title: Dilution: when invoices shrink
body: Dilution is any reduction in an invoice's value that is not a credit loss: credit notes for returns, quality discounts, rebates, pricing errors. A barley supplier invoices ETB 120,000, but the malt plant finds high moisture and pays ETB 112,000. The ETB 8,000 is dilution.

In receivables discounting and factoring, the bank lends before final settlement, so it holds a dilution reserve: a share of each receivable it does not advance. The reserve is set from the debtor's history, usually from the highest monthly dilution rather than the average.

parts.label: Credit notes and deductions in the month
Invoices issued in the same month

visual.caption: Track it monthly and per debtor; size reserves from the worst months.

worked.title: Receivables discounting for a Meskerem distributor (ETB million)

rows.label: Receivables ledger of Kebede Beverage Distribution PLC
Less ineligible: over 90 days or disputed

worked.note: Kebede can draw up to about ETB 6.7 million against its current ledger; the figure falls if dilution rises.

scenario.title: Rising rejections
scenario.situation: In the rainy season Meskerem rejects more barley: credit notes rise from 3% of supplier invoices to 6.5% in August. Some suppliers outside the payables programme use a receivables discounting line at Bank A against their invoices to Meskerem.
scenario.question: What should Bank A do for the discounting line?
options: Nothing, because Meskerem is a strong buyer
Raise the dilution reserve for the season and fund only after goods are graded
Raise the advance rate to help suppliers
scenario.explain: Dilution is not credit risk: Meskerem may be strong and still pay less. A higher seasonal reserve, or funding only after grading and approval, protects the bank while keeping suppliers financed.

lessons.title: True sale or recourse, and the Ethiopian legal steps
body: In a true sale, the supplier sells the receivable outright; if the buyer does not pay, the bank's claim is on the buyer, not the supplier. With recourse, the bank can claim back from the supplier. Payables finance is normally without recourse to the supplier because the anchor's undertaking is the security. Receivables discounting for SMEs is usually with recourse.

In Ethiopia, banks document the assignment of receivables by contract, give written notice to the debtor so it pays only the bank, and register the security right in the Movable Collateral Registry. Whether a structure is a true sale for accounting and insolvency purposes is a legal and accounting question: ask the bank's legal and finance units before promising suppliers a non-recourse product.

left.title: Without recourse (true sale)
items: Bank bears the buyer's credit risk
Supplier gets cash and removes the receivable

right.title: With recourse
items: Supplier repays if the buyer does not
Receivable stays on supplier's books with a liability
Priced on supplier and buyer risk

regulation.source: Movable Property Security Right Proclamation No. 1147/2019, as cited in a commercial bank's credit manual
regulation.text: Movable property that can secure a loan includes inventories, agricultural products, receivables and other incorporeal assets, and warehouse receipts. A typical Ethiopian bank manual requires security rights over movables to be registered in the Ethiopian Movable Collateral Registry, operational since 26 February 2020 under NBE Directive MCR/01/2020.

lessons.tip: An assignment the buyer has not been notified of is weak: the buyer can still pay the supplier and be discharged.

lessons.title: Structuring limits
body: Programme finance has layered limits: a programme limit on the anchor, sublimits by supplier segment, caps per supplier, and a maximum tenor per invoice. Each layer answers a different risk: anchor default, concentration, operational overload and terms creeping longer than agreed.
All exposures to the anchor group must be added together, including its overdraft, term loans, guarantees, L/Cs and the programme limit, before testing the regulatory large exposure cap.

worked.title: Meskerem group exposure at Bank A (ETB million)

rows.label: Existing overdraft, term loan and L/C lines

worked.note: The new limit makes Meskerem a large exposure, reported monthly, but well inside the 25% cap.

points: Programme limit ETB 400 million on Meskerem
SME supplier cap ETB 20 million each; smallholder cap ETB 500,000 each
Maximum invoice tenor 90 days from delivery; no rollovers
Limit review every 12 months, or sooner on a covenant breach

scenario.title: A request to double the limit
scenario.situation: Six months in, Meskerem asks Bank A to raise the programme to ETB 800 million so it can move suppliers to 120 days. Its group exposure would rise to ETB 1,900 million.
scenario.question: What is the main issue for the credit team?
options: The longer terms stretch suppliers and turn more of Meskerem's payables into bank exposure, which needs fresh anchor analysis
There is no issue as long as uptake stays at 60%
scenario.explain: ETB 1,900 million is 15.8% of capital, inside the cap. The real question is credit: moving to 120 days is a bigger bet on Meskerem's cash and may hurt suppliers who choose not to discount.

lessons.title: Risk-based pricing and defending price
body: Since NBE/INT/13/2026, Ethiopian banks set lending rates freely. A programme discount rate is built from the bank's cost of funds, operating cost, expected loss on the anchor, a charge for the capital the exposure uses, and a profit margin. Because the risk is the anchor's, the rate should be well below what an SME pays on its own overdraft.

Defend the price by showing value, not by cutting the margin. The supplier compares the discount with its real alternatives: its own overdraft, a trader paying cash at a lower price, or an informal lender.

regulation.source: NBE Directive NBE/INT/13/2026, Interest rates (as amended)
regulation.text: Banks set deposit and lending rates freely; there is no minimum deposit rate, and banks report rates to the NBE within set working days. Programme discount rates are therefore a commercial decision, which makes a clear and documented pricing method more important.

worked.title: Meskerem programme discount rate and a supplier's cost

rows.label: SME invoice ETB 1,000,000 paid 80 days early: discount 1,000,000 x 17% x 80 / 365
Same funding on the SME's own overdraft at 22%

worked.note: The supplier saves almost ETB 11,000 per million and does not need to pledge collateral.

scenario.title: A cheaper competitor
scenario.situation: Tigist Haile, finance manager of Addis Crown Cork PLC, says another bank offers to discount her Meskerem invoices at 15.5%, with full recourse and a building pledge.
scenario.question: What is Bank A's strongest response?
options: Explain that Bank A's 17% is without recourse and needs no collateral, so the true cost comparison favours the programme
Tell her the other bank is not allowed to price below 17%
scenario.explain: Price must be compared on the same terms. Recourse and a building pledge cost the supplier risk and capacity. Rates are free under NBE/INT/13/2026, so there is no regulatory floor to invoke.

example.title: A farmer's early payment
example.text: Gemechu Tola delivers 20 quintals of malting barley worth ETB 120,000. Approved on day 5, it is due on day 90. If he takes early payment for the 85 days at 17%, the discount is about ETB 4,751 and he receives ETB 115,249 within two days. A local trader had offered him cash at ETB 5,400 a quintal, or ETB 108,000.

takeaways: In payables finance every approved invoice is an exposure on the anchor; test its cash without the stretch
Performance and fraud risk are managed mainly by approval before funding and system controls
Dilution is not a credit loss; size reserves from the worst months and per debtor
Assignment needs a contract, notice to the debtor and registration in the Movable Collateral Registry
Add all group exposures before testing the 25% cap; price on the anchor's risk and defend on value

quiz.explain: Reductions for quality, returns or pricing are dilution, not default.

quiz.q: Eligible receivables are ETB 8.8 million, the dilution reserve is 5% and the advance rate is 80%. Maximum availability is about
In a true sale of receivables without recourse, if the buyer fails to pay
options: The anchor's suppliers share the loss
The supplier must repay the bank
The bank bears the loss and claims on the buyer
quiz.explain: Without recourse, the bank has bought the buyer's risk.

quiz.q: Bank A has total capital of ETB 12 billion. What is the maximum exposure to one group under SBB/87/2024?
quiz.explain: 25% of ETB 12 billion is ETB 3 billion.

quiz.q: Why should a programme rate be lower than the supplier's overdraft rate?
options: Because the risk priced is mainly the stronger anchor's
Because the NBE sets a ceiling
quiz.explain: Payables finance is priced on the anchor's credit, which is usually stronger than the SME's.

quiz.q: Which control best prevents the same invoice being financed twice?
options: Unique invoice numbering and automatic duplicate checks on the platform
quiz.explain: Duplicate financing is an operational fraud risk, stopped by system checks.

modules.title: Commodity and inventory finance
modules.summary: Lend against goods you control: register the security, contract a collateral manager, monitor the warehouse, margin the loan and use ECX warehouse receipts.
objectives: Describe how security over inventory and warehouse receipts is created, registered and enforced in Ethiopia
Set up a collateral management agreement and a warehouse monitoring routine
Value pledged commodities, set advance rates and calculate a margin call
Use ECX electronic warehouse receipts for finance, from pledge to foreclosure

lessons.title: The legal basis for inventory and receipt finance
body: Inventory finance only works if the bank's right over the goods is clear and enforceable. Ethiopia's Movable Property Security Right Proclamation No. 1147/2019 allows security over inventories, agricultural products and warehouse receipts, and the online Movable Collateral Registry gives the bank a public, time-stamped priority.

Warehouse receipts add a second layer. Under the Warehouse Receipt System Proclamation No. 372/2003, as a typical bank manual describes it, possession of goods by an agreed third party warehouse is as good as the creditor's own possession. That is why a bank can lend against barley or sesame it never touches.

items.label: Pledge agreement
items.text: Borrower grants a security right over named goods or receipts

items.label: Registry filing
items.text: Bank registers the right in the Movable Collateral Registry

items.label: Control
items.text: Goods held under dual lock, a collateral manager or an ECX pledge

items.label: Monitoring
items.text: Stock reports, visits and price checks during the loan

items.label: Enforcement
items.text: On default, sale of the goods or receipts and application of proceeds

regulation.source: NBE Directive MCR/01/2020, as described in a commercial bank's credit manual
regulation.text: Security rights over movables, shares and cash collateral are registered in the Ethiopian Movable Collateral Registry System, operational from 26 February 2020. The manual also records that the directive asks banks to allocate at least 5% of annual disbursements to agriculture and MSMEs using movable property as collateral.

example.title: A lost priority
example.text: Bale Grain Traders PLC pledged 4,000 quintals of wheat to two lenders in one month. Bank A had a signed pledge but filed in the registry a week late; the other lender filed first and took priority over the goods. Bank A's credit administration now files on the day the pledge is signed and before disbursement.

lessons.title: Collateral management agreements
body: When goods sit in the borrower's or a third party's warehouse, the bank needs someone it trusts at the door. A collateral management agreement is a tripartite contract between the bank, the borrower and a collateral manager or warehouse operator. The manager holds the goods to the bank's order, releases them only on the bank's written instruction and reports stock regularly.

A typical Ethiopian bank manual sets the basics: goods in a warehouse with a cement screed floor, ventilation and no other entrance than dual-locked doors, sealed, insured against fire, lightning and burglary, and all custody costs, including the salary of the bank's controlling staff, borne by the borrower.

items.label: Bank
items.text: Lender; issues release instructions; monitors and values

items.label: Borrower
items.text: Owns the goods; pays custody costs and insurance

items.label: Collateral manager
items.text: Holds goods to the bank's order; releases only on instruction

items.label: Insurer
items.text: Covers fire, lightning, burglary and transit, endorsed to the bank

scenario.title: Which collateral to accept
scenario.situation: Arsi Barley Union, which aggregates barley from member cooperatives for Meskerem, asks Bank A for ETB 30 million to pay farmers at harvest before deliveries to the malt plant. It offers three options: a stock list without control, barley in its own warehouse under a collateral manager, or a guarantee from a board member.
scenario.question: Which structure fits best?
options: Barley under a collateral management agreement in a warehouse meeting the bank's standards
The board member's personal guarantee alone
No security, since Meskerem will buy the barley
scenario.explain: A manual typically treats stock-list finance as close to a clean loan. Controlled, insured stock under a tripartite agreement gives the bank real security, and the union's sales to Meskerem become the repayment source.

lessons.tip: Read the release clause twice: the whole value of a collateral manager is that nothing leaves without the bank's instruction.

lessons.title: Warehouse monitoring and stock reconciliation
body: Controlled goods can still disappear: through theft, through releases without instruction, or because the stock was never there. A typical bank manual asks for a fortnightly status report from the controlling staff and a monthly visit by the bank, and for physical counts reconciled with the stock register.

The reconciliation is simple arithmetic: opening stock plus receipts minus authorised releases should equal physical stock. Any shortfall is a warning sign, even when the remaining stock still covers the loan.

rows.label: Less releases to Meskerem on bank instruction
Value of physical stock at ETB 6,000 per quintal (assumed)

worked.note: The loan is still covered, but a 350 quintal gap needs an explanation in writing before the next release.

scenario.title: A gap in the count
scenario.situation: The reconciliation above shows 350 quintals missing. The union manager, Lemma Girma, says the barley was moved to a drying yard during rain and will return within a week.
scenario.question: What is the right response?
options: Accept the explanation because coverage is still about 69%
Stop further releases, inspect the drying yard with the collateral manager and record the stock there under control
Increase the loan to cover drying costs
scenario.explain: Goods moved without instruction break the control the bank relies on. Verifying and bringing the stock back under control comes first; calling the loan is premature if the explanation checks out.

lessons.title: Valuation, advance rates and margin calls
body: Pledged goods are valued at the lower of cost or market. A typical Ethiopian bank manual caps merchandise advances at 80% of that value, uses about 70% for warehouse receipts and un-cleaned exportables, and allows 80%, exceptionally 85%, for exportable commodities ready for export.

The gap between value and loan is the margin. When prices fall, the margin shrinks. The manual asks the borrower to add goods or cash so that the value stays 20% above the loan balance for merchandise, and for warehouse receipts to top up when the market value falls below the balance.

visual.caption: Advance rates in a typical Ethiopian bank manual; each bank sets its own.

example.title: Merchandise valuation in practice
example.text: Hawassa Steel Traders PLC pledges imported reinforcement bars. Landed cost, excluding VAT, is ETB 47.1 million and the current market value ETB 65 million. Bank A values the stock at the lower figure, ETB 47.1 million, and at a 70% advance lends about ETB 33.0 million. The higher market value is a cushion, not a basis for lending more.

lessons.title: ECX warehouse receipts: pledge to foreclosure
body: Ethiopian Commodity Exchange receipts are the most standardised commodity collateral in the country. ECX grades and stores the commodity, issues an electronic warehouse receipt and, once the bank pledges it, sets a No-Sale status that cannot change without the bank's consent. The bank checks prices weekly.

A typical bank manual sets the loan tenor to end 15 days before the receipt expires: sesame stored 90 days gets a 75 day loan. Value uses the lower of the latest ECX price and the one-year average. Repayment is from the borrower's own funds or from an ECX sale, with ECX remitting proceeds to the bank.

regulation.source: A commercial bank's credit procedure manual (2025)
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual finances only ECX members or clients against ECX receipts, advances up to 70% of the lower of the latest ECX price and the one-year average, sets a minimum loan of ETB 150,000, and ends the loan 15 days before the receipt expires (for example sesame 90 days storage, 75 days loan; wheat 120 days, 105 days). On default it gives a 15-day notice, then a 5-day final notice, then instructs ECX to sell, with the sale to be completed within 35 days.

worked.title: Sesame receipt loan and a falling price (ETB)

rows.label: Value at the lower price: 3,000 x 13,800
Value if price falls to 9,500: 3,000 x 9,500

worked.note: On the weekly check, value has fallen below the balance; the borrower must add cash or collateral as the loan contract requires.

items.label: Day 0
items.text: Receipt pledged; ECX sets No-Sale

items.label: Weekly
items.text: Bank checks ECX prices against the balance

items.label: Loan expiry
items.text: 15-day notice if unpaid

items.label: Receipt expiry
items.text: 5-day final notice

items.label: Foreclosure
items.text: Bank instructs ECX sale, completed within 35 days

scenario.title: Peak season prices
scenario.situation: In peak season the latest ECX sesame price is 25% above the one-year average and well above local market prices. A trader asks Bank A to value his receipts at the latest price.
scenario.question: What should Bank A use?
options: The latest ECX price, since it is the official price
The lower of the latest price and the one-year average, or a local or lowest-year price if the ECX price looks inflated
The highest price of the year
The trader's purchase price, whatever it was
scenario.explain: Valuation is conservative by design: the lower of the two prices, with room to use lower local or yearly prices when the exchange price is temporarily inflated.

lessons.title: Running case: financing barley before it reaches Meskerem
body: Payables finance only starts once Meskerem approves an invoice. Before that, farmers and their union need cash at harvest. Bank A closes the gap with an inventory facility to Arsi Barley Union, secured by barley under a collateral management agreement and repaid from Meskerem's approved invoices for the union's deliveries.

The two products connect: when the union delivers to Meskerem, the approved invoice is either paid early under the programme or paid at maturity, and the proceeds go first to the inventory facility. Bank A sees the barley from the farm gate to the malt plant.

example.title: Paying farmers at harvest
example.text: In the first season Arsi Barley Union drew ETB 28 million in three phases, each released only after the previous lot was in the warehouse. Farmers were paid into their accounts within a week of grading instead of waiting two months. Releases to Meskerem matched approved invoices, and the facility was fully repaid 70 days after the last draw.

takeaways: Register every pledge in the Movable Collateral Registry before disbursing; priority goes to the first filing
A tripartite collateral management agreement turns stored goods into controlled collateral
Reconcile book and physical stock every month; any unexplained gap stops releases
Value at the lower of cost or market and maintain the margin when prices fall
ECX receipts offer standardised grading, a No-Sale pledge and a defined foreclosure path

quiz.q: Why must a pledge over inventory be registered before disbursement?
options: Because priority among lenders follows registration in the Movable Collateral Registry
Because ECX requires it for all goods
To transfer ownership to the bank
quiz.explain: Registration gives public notice and priority.

quiz.q: Sesame is stored at ECX for 90 days. Under the manual's rule, the loan tenor is
quiz.explain: The loan ends 15 days before the receipt expires.

quiz.q: A 3,000 quintal sesame receipt has a latest price of ETB 14,500 and a one-year average of ETB 13,800. At 70%, the loan is
quiz.explain: Use the lower price: 3,000 x 13,800 x 70% = ETB 28.98 million.

quiz.q: Book stock is 7,100 quintals and the physical count is 6,750. What should happen first?
options: Release more stock to keep the borrower happy
Stop releases and investigate the 350 quintal gap
quiz.explain: Unexplained shortfalls are a control failure, whatever the remaining coverage.

quiz.q: Who normally bears warehouse custody costs, including the bank's controlling staff salary, under a typical Ethiopian bank manual?
quiz.explain: The manual puts all custodial costs on the borrower.

quiz.q: What does the No-Sale status on an ECX receipt achieve?
options: It transfers the goods to the bank
It stops the receipt being sold without the bank's consent
quiz.explain: The pledge flag protects the bank's control over the receipt.

modules.title: Export and import supply chain finance
modules.summary: Finance exporters from contract to proceeds and importers from L/C to distributor, within Ethiopia's foreign exchange rules on repatriation, retention and payment modes.
objectives: Apply FXD/01/2024 and its amendments on repatriation, conversion, retention and import payment modes to SCF structures
Structure pre-shipment finance and advances against export bills, and plan repayment from proceeds
Structure import and distributor finance, including goods in transit
Identify FX, logistics and retention account risks and the controls for each

lessons.title: The foreign exchange rules that shape trade SCF
body: Every export or import SCF structure in Ethiopia runs inside the foreign exchange framework. FXD/01/2024 introduced market-based rates and set the rules for export proceeds: repatriation within three months, conversion of part of the proceeds to Birr and retention of the rest in a foreign currency retention account.

Later amendments matter for structuring. FXD/04/2026 allows banks to offer forward rates and lets service exporters retain 100% of proceeds. FXD/05/2026 lets banks approve L/Cs on acceptance and cash against documents on acceptance without prior NBE approval for holders of foreign currency or retention accounts. At MPC meeting No. 7 in July 2026 the NBE announced a cut in the surrender requirement on goods exports from 50% to 30%; check the implementing directive before relying on the new share.

regulation.source: NBE Directive FXD/01/2024, Foreign exchange (as amended by FXD/04/2026 and FXD/05/2026)
regulation.text: Exporters must repatriate proceeds within three months, convert 50% to Birr and may keep 50% in a retention account (MPC No. 7 announced a cut of the goods-export surrender share to 30%). Banks may offer forward contracts and, since May 2026, may approve L/Cs on acceptance and cash against documents on acceptance without prior NBE approval for foreign currency and retention account holders, pricing L/C fees on an annualised basis pro-rated to tenor.

items.label: Contract
items.text: Sales contract registered or authenticated; L/C or other payment mode agreed

items.label: Pre-shipment
items.text: Bank advances Birr to buy and prepare goods

items.label: Shipment
items.text: Goods move through Djibouti; documents to the buyer's bank

items.label: Proceeds
items.text: Repatriated within three months to the exporter's account

items.label: Split
items.text: Part converted to Birr, the rest retained; advance repaid

lessons.tip: Always write in the facility letter which part of the proceeds repays the advance, and that the exporter authorises conversion from retention if needed.

lessons.title: Pre-shipment finance for coffee and oilseeds
body: Pre-shipment finance gives the exporter Birr to buy, clean and bag goods for a specific contract. A typical Ethiopian bank manual advances up to 80% of the export value against a coffee sales contract with an NBE-authenticated price and up to 90% against an L/C. For sesame and other non-coffee goods it allows up to 80% with immovable collateral, otherwise 70%.

Controls follow the money. For ECX commodities the advance is paid to the exporter's ECX pay-in account, so it can only buy the commodity. The L/C must be opened and shipment completed within 90 days, exports must be channelled through the bank, and the exporter must not be on the NBE's delinquent exporter list.

regulation.source: A commercial bank's credit procedure manual (2025)
regulation.text: A typical bank manual requires for coffee pre-shipment an original sales contract with an NBE-authenticated price and the exporter's previous export performance; for cereals and oilseeds a contract authenticated by the Ministry of Trade and an export record in the same commodity and market. No second advance may be made on the same contract, and older advances due for shipment must be cleared first.

scenario.title: Advance on a sales contract
scenario.situation: Sidra Highland Coffee Export PLC has an NBE-authenticated sales contract for USD 600,000 of washed Sidama coffee with a Hamburg roaster, payment by L/C still to be opened. Its owner, Yonas Desta, asks for 90% now.
scenario.question: What can Bank A offer under the manual's rules?
options: 90% now, since the buyer is reputable
Up to 80% now on the contract, with the further 10% once the L/C is opened
Nothing until goods are at Djibouti
scenario.explain: Coffee on a sales contract gets up to 80%; the extra 10% follows when the L/C is opened through the bank.

example.title: Paying into the ECX account
example.text: Sesame exporter Metema Agro Export PLC asked for its pre-shipment advance in its current account to pay a truck owner. Bank A paid the advance to its ECX pay-in account instead and arranged a separate small overdraft for transport. The rule keeps the advance tied to the commodity that will be shipped.

lessons.title: Export receivables and repayment from proceeds
body: Once goods are on their way, the exporter's need moves to the receivable. An advance against export bills lets the exporter draw on presentation of export documents other than the bill of lading. A typical manual allows up to 80% of the bill, each advance up to 90 days, for exporters with a clean track record and no pre-shipment advance on the same contract.

Plan repayment carefully. If the advance was paid in Birr and only part of the proceeds is converted automatically, the converted Birr may not cover principal and interest. The exporter must convert part of its retained foreign currency, which should be agreed at the start.

worked.title: Sidra coffee: repaying an 80% pre-shipment advance

rows.label: Contract value USD 600,000 at ETB 150 per USD (assumed)

worked.note: With a lower mandatory conversion share, more must come from retention; the facility letter must give the bank the right to convert it.

left.title: Documentary credit (L/C)
items: Buyer's bank undertakes to pay on compliant documents
Lower risk; strongest basis for pre-shipment

right.title: Collection or open account
items: Buyer pays on documents or on credit terms
Risk on the buyer alone unless insured
Cheaper and faster for the buyer
Needs buyer knowledge, insurance or both

scenario.title: A cheaper payment mode
scenario.situation: A long-standing Belgian buyer asks Sidra to drop the L/C and move to cash against documents to save cost. Sidra's pre-shipment line was approved on L/C terms.
scenario.question: What should Bank A do?
options: Ask Sidra to ship without documents
Accept automatically, since the buyer is long-standing
Re-assess: under the manual, advances on sales contracts need L/C terms unless a senior committee approves an exception, possibly with credit insurance
Refuse all future finance to Sidra
scenario.explain: The payment mode is part of the credit decision. A change needs a fresh assessment and, under a typical manual, senior approval; credit insurance on the buyer can support it.

lessons.title: Import finance: L/Cs, goods in transit and what not to pledge
body: Fuel, fertiliser and medicines are Ethiopia's critical import chains, and most of Meskerem's hops, bottles and spare parts are imported too. A typical bank manual lets an importer open L/Cs within a facility on a margin of at least 30% of the L/C value, citing FXD/01/2024, with each advance on import bills running 90 days.

Goods in transit can be financed for up to 90 days under a tripartite agreement between the bank, the importer and a bank-accepted transitor, with insurance from the port of discharge to the importer's warehouse and the goods then held under dual control. Not everything is good collateral: the same manual excludes perishable and short-life goods, such as pharmaceuticals, packed foods and chemicals, as merchandise pledges.

items.label: L/C opened
items.text: Importer pays the margin; bank issues the L/C

items.label: Documents arrive
items.text: Bank checks for discrepancies; advance on import bill if needed

items.label: Transit
items.text: Transitor clears through Djibouti under a tripartite agreement

items.label: Warehouse
items.text: Goods under dual control, insured, checked against invoice

items.label: Sale
items.text: Releases against payment; advance settled within 90 days

scenario.title: A pharmaceutical importer's stock
scenario.situation: Medhin Pharmaceuticals Import PLC asks Bank A to pledge ETB 40 million of imported medicines, mostly with 10 to 14 months to expiry, against an import bill advance.
scenario.question: How should the officer treat the medicines?
options: As ideal collateral, since medicines are essential
As unacceptable merchandise collateral under the manual, so look for other repayment support such as receivables from hospitals or other security
scenario.explain: Essential is not the same as good collateral. Pharmaceuticals and goods with under a year to expiry are excluded as merchandise pledges in a typical manual; the bank can look instead at the importer's receivables or other security.

lessons.title: Distributor finance on the anchor's sales side
body: An anchor can support its buyers as well as its suppliers. Meskerem sells through 40 distributors who pay cash on collection and often run short of stock in peak season. Distributor finance lets each distributor buy from Meskerem on bank credit, repaid from its sales within a short period.

A typical Ethiopian bank manual describes a supplier-distributor special overdraft: separate 30-day contracts are booked for each purchase from the supplier, and the supplier may pay part of the interest under an agreement with the bank. Meskerem can also agree to stop supplying a distributor that is overdue, which gives the bank strong leverage.

worked.title: Distributor finance with interest sharing (ETB)

rows.label: Monthly purchases from Meskerem by Kebede Beverage Distribution PLC
30-day contract limit: one month of purchases

worked.note: Meskerem buys faster sales and loyalty for about ETB 24,700 a month per distributor; the bank keeps a full 17% yield.

example.title: A stop-supply clause at work
example.text: When Wolaita Sodo Beverage Distributors PLC missed two 30-day contracts, Meskerem paused its deliveries under the programme agreement until the arrears were paid. The distributor cleared the ETB 4.2 million within ten days, because without stock it had nothing to sell.

lessons.title: FX, logistics and retention risks
body: Trade SCF carries risks a domestic programme does not. Exchange rates now move freely, so a Birr advance repaid from foreign proceeds, or an import bill repaid in Birr, changes cost as the rate moves. Forward contracts, allowed since FXD/04/2026, can fix the rate for a known receipt or payment.

Logistics through Djibouti adds time: port congestion, trucking delays and customs holds can push a shipment past the 90-day shipment window or the repatriation deadline. Build realistic days into tenors and require insurance from the warehouse to the named port for exports, as a typical manual does.

items.label: Exchange rate
items.text: Birr cost of import bills rises when the Birr weakens; consider forwards

items.label: Logistics
items.text: Djibouti corridor delays can breach shipment or repatriation windows

items.label: Retention balances
items.text: Exporter may spend retained FX elsewhere; agree conversion rights up front

items.label: Buyer and country
items.text: Foreign buyer default or sanctions; check buyer and insure

scenario.title: A delayed vessel
scenario.situation: Metema Agro Export's sesame shipment is stuck at Djibouti for three weeks. The pre-shipment advance's 90-day shipment deadline is in ten days, and the buyer's L/C expires in 25 days.
scenario.question: What is the best first action for Bank A?
options: Ask the exporter to seek an L/C extension from the buyer now, document the delay and agree a short extension within approval authority
Convert the exporter's retention balance without asking
scenario.explain: Logistics delays are common and manageable if acted on early. An L/C amendment and a documented extension protect both the trade and the bank; default or unilateral conversion would be premature.

takeaways: Export SCF runs inside FXD/01/2024: three-month repatriation, a conversion share and retention, now amended by FXD/04/2026, FXD/05/2026 and the MPC No. 7 decision
Pre-shipment advances are tied to an authenticated contract or L/C and paid into the ECX pay-in account for ECX goods
Plan repayment from proceeds: the converted share may not cover the advance, so secure rights over retention
Import finance uses L/C margins, 90-day import bills and tripartite transit agreements; not every import is good collateral
Distributor finance with interest sharing and stop-supply clauses extends the anchor's strength to its sales side

quiz.q: Within what period must export proceeds be repatriated under FXD/01/2024?
quiz.explain: The directive requires repatriation within three months.

quiz.q: Under a typical bank manual, what is the maximum pre-shipment advance against a coffee sales contract, before an L/C is opened?
quiz.explain: Up to 80% on the contract, with a further 10% once the L/C is opened.

quiz.q: An advance of ETB 72 million plus ETB 2.5 million interest is repaid from proceeds of ETB 90 million, of which 50% is converted. How much must come from retained foreign currency?
quiz.explain: 74.5 minus 45 = about ETB 29.5 million.

quiz.q: Which directive lets banks approve L/Cs on acceptance without prior NBE approval for retention account holders?
quiz.explain: FXD/05/2026, effective 25 May 2026.

quiz.q: Why are pharmaceuticals poor merchandise collateral in a typical manual?
options: They have limited shelf life and are excluded as perishable or short-life goods
quiz.explain: Goods with short shelf life or under a year to expiry are excluded.

quiz.q: In the supplier-distributor overdraft, what gives the bank strong leverage over distributors?
options: The anchor's agreement to stop supplying overdue distributors
quiz.explain: A distributor without stock has no sales, so the stop-supply clause encourages prompt repayment.

modules.title: Risk mitigation, technology and the programme capstone
modules.summary: Share risk with insurers, guarantors and trade finance lines, run the programme on data and digital payments, and present the Meskerem programme design.
objectives: Use credit insurance, partial credit guarantees and DFI or multilateral trade lines to extend SCF to riskier segments
Choose SCF technology, e-invoicing and digital farmer payments that fit Ethiopian rules and infrastructure
Monitor a live programme with key indicators and apply provisioning when payments slip
Design and defend a complete payables finance programme for a large anchor and its suppliers

lessons.title: Credit and goods insurance
body: Two kinds of insurance support SCF. Goods insurance protects the collateral: a typical bank manual asks for pledged stock to be insured against fire, lightning and burglary, and for goods in transit to be covered from the warehouse to the port for exports, or from the port of discharge to the warehouse for imports, with the policy endorsed to the bank.

Credit insurance protects the receivable: it pays if a buyer fails to pay for insolvency or delay. For exporters selling on collection or open account, insurance on the foreign buyer can make an advance against export bills bankable. Check the policy's exclusions, waiting period and the share of loss it covers.

left.title: Goods insurance
items: Covers loss of or damage to the goods

right.title: Credit insurance
items: Covers the buyer's failure to pay

example.title: Insurance that made a deal
example.text: Ziway Roses Export PLC sold flowers to an auction buyer on 30-day open account and could not get an advance without an L/C. With credit insurance covering 85% of the buyer's risk and Bank A named as loss payee, the bank advanced 70% of each invoice. When the buyer paid late one winter, the policy covered the gap.

lessons.title: Partial credit guarantees and trade finance lines
body: A partial credit guarantee from a development finance institution covers a share of the bank's losses on a defined portfolio, such as input loans to smallholders or SME supplier advances. It lets the bank lend to segments it would otherwise avoid, but the bank still carries part of the loss and must follow the guarantor's rules exactly, or the cover can fail.

A typical bank manual describes an export credit guarantee scheme under NBE Directive SBB/41/2007, provided through a state development finance institution, covering 80% of the outstanding balance and interest on eligible pre- and post-shipment advances. Multilateral providers such as Afreximbank and ITFC offer trade finance lines and guarantees to African banks, which can fund or de-risk import and export programmes.

worked.title: Barley input loans with a 50% partial credit guarantee (ETB million)

rows.label: Input loans to Meskerem's smallholders, repaid from barley deliveries
Guarantee fee at 1.5% of the portfolio (assumed)
Net saving before any capital benefit

worked.note: The guarantee halves the expected loss for a modest net saving; its larger value is the confidence to lend to farmers without buildings.

scenario.title: A guarantee claim at risk
scenario.situation: Bank A's guarantor requires every guaranteed loan to be reported within 30 days of disbursement. An audit finds 40 farmer loans reported after 60 days.
scenario.question: What is the main risk?
options: None, since the loans are performing
The guarantor may refuse to cover those loans, so the bank's real protection is lower than it thinks
The NBE will cancel the loans
scenario.explain: Guarantees protect only when their conditions are met. Late reporting can void cover on those loans, so compliance with guarantor rules is a core control.

lessons.title: Platforms, e-invoicing and digital payments to farmers
body: Technology turns SCF from a document process into a data process. The anchor's ERP sends approved invoices to the platform, suppliers accept early payment on a phone or web screen, and the bank pays into the supplier's account the same day. Electronic records and signatures have legal standing under Ethiopia's electronic transaction law, and supplier data must be handled under the personal data protection law.

Paying farmers digitally reduces cash handling and builds a payment history the bank can later use to lend. Check the limits of the channel: mobile money wallets carry daily balance and transaction limits, so large barley payments may need to go to a bank account.

regulation.source: NBE Directive ONPS/09/2023, Payment instrument issuer (amendment), as announced
regulation.text: The NBE raised the daily wallet balance limit for mobile money from Birr 30,000 to Birr 75,000 and set a daily aggregate transaction limit of Birr 150,000, with exemptions such as utility, tax and bulk payments. Later amendments may apply; confirm current limits before designing farmer payment flows.

scenario.title: Paying Gemechu
scenario.situation: Gemechu Tola's early payment of ETB 115,249 is ready. He has a mobile money wallet and a basic bank account opened at the field day. Meskerem asks Bank A to pay all farmers to wallets because it is simpler.
scenario.question: What should Bank A do?
options: Split the payment over several days to the wallet without telling him
Pay the whole amount to the wallet
Pay into his bank account, keeping wallets for smaller payments within the limits
scenario.explain: ETB 115,249 is above the Birr 75,000 wallet balance limit announced under ONPS/09/2023. The bank account avoids a failed payment, and cash would lose the data and safety benefits.

items.label: ERP upload
items.text: Meskerem's system sends approved invoices daily

items.label: Supplier offer
items.text: Supplier sees amount, discount and payment date

items.label: Acceptance
items.text: One click or SMS reply; electronic record kept

items.label: Payment
items.text: Same-day credit to account or wallet within limits

items.label: Settlement
items.text: Meskerem pays Bank A the full face value on the due date

lessons.title: Monitoring a live programme and provisioning
body: A programme needs a monthly dashboard: uptake, average days financed, anchor payments on time, dilution, concentration by supplier, and suppliers onboarded versus planned. A late anchor payment is the single most important warning: it means the obligor behind every invoice is under strain.

Programme exposures are loans and are classified and provisioned like other credit. Under SBB/90/2024, provisions are 1% for pass, 3% for special mention, 20% for substandard, 50% for doubtful and 100% for loss, and non-performing exposures stop accruing interest.

worked.title: Provisioning when part of the programme slips (ETB million)

rows.label: Invoices moved to special mention after late anchor payments

worked.note: A small slip adds ETB 0.4 million of provision; the bigger signal is the change in the anchor's behaviour.

regulation.source: NBE Directive SBB/90/2024, Asset classification and provisioning
regulation.text: Provisions are pass 1%, special mention 3%, substandard 20%, doubtful 50% and loss 100%. Interest on non-performing loans is not accrued, and any shortfall of IFRS impairment against the regulatory provision goes to a regulatory reserve.

visual.caption: Meskerem's programme terms; a rise in average days financed above target is a monitoring trigger.

lessons.title: Capstone: the Meskerem programme design
body: Teams now bring the course together into a programme design for Meskerem and its 300 suppliers, to be presented to Bank A's credit committee. The design must cover the anchor, eligibility and onboarding, limits and pricing, risk controls, technology and how smallholders are financed before and after delivery.

The committee will test three things: whether the bank is really taking Meskerem's risk and no other, whether the suppliers gain enough to join, and whether the controls would catch a fake, duplicate or disputed invoice.

worked.title: Meskerem payables finance: summary term sheet

rows.label: Invoice tenor
rows.value: Up to 90 days from delivery, no rollovers

rows.label: Anchor undertaking
rows.value: Irrevocable, full face value, no set-off after approval

rows.label: Recourse
rows.value: None to suppliers on approved invoices

rows.label: Upstream finance
rows.value: Inventory facility to Arsi Barley Union under a CMA

rows.label: Key covenant
rows.value: Meskerem net debt / EBITDA at most 2.5x

rows.label: Payments
rows.value: To supplier bank accounts; wallets within limits

worked.note: This is the backbone of the programme design assessment; teams add controls, KPIs and a roll-out plan.

scenario.title: The committee's hardest question
scenario.situation: A committee member, Ato Solomon Getachew, asks: if Meskerem is late paying the bank on a Friday maturity, what happens to the 300 suppliers who were paid early?
scenario.question: Which answer reflects the programme design?
options: The bank debits the farmers' accounts
The suppliers must refund the bank
Nothing changes for suppliers who were paid early; the bank claims on Meskerem under its undertaking and stops new financing until it pays
scenario.explain: Without recourse, the early-paid suppliers keep their money. The bank's remedy is against the anchor, and new purchases stop until Meskerem pays.

lessons.title: Work assignment: an SCF opportunity in your own portfolio
body: The course ends back at work. Each learner identifies one supply chain finance opportunity among their own customers: an anchor whose suppliers wait for cash, an exporter financing purchases on overdraft, an importer with distributors, or a trader with stock that could sit in a controlled warehouse.

Write a two-page note: the chain, the gap, the product, the main risk and control, an indicative limit and price, and what the customer and the bank gain. Your manager or a trade finance specialist reviews it against the course framework.
